sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: On-Site Factory Pre-Shipment Quality Control and Audit Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (predominantly Civil Law, with Common Law-inspired commercial statutes, notably the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by the 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1983, as amended by the 2014 Protocol)
BLEU–Hong Kong Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1996, applicable to Luxembourg)
EU–Singapore Free Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement (applicable in Luxembourg since 2019/2022)
EU–Vietnam Free Trade Agreement and EU–Vietnam Investment Protection Agreement (applicable in Luxembourg since 2019/2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 (SCSp regime); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 4 December 2020 (implementation of AML Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 17 June 2020 on RBE filings; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT. UBO declaration must be lodged with the RBE within one month of RCSL registration; failure is punishable by fines (EUR 125–1,250 per entity).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or official registry extract of the foreign corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the General Partner's country of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Secretary of State, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg acceded with effect from 3 June 1979; accepted for all contracting states) OR consular legalization for non-Apostille countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same competent registry or tax administration as per origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (or constitutive deed) of the foreign corporate General Partner, certified as a true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin registry or notary public of the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney executed by the General Partner and each Limited Partner authorizing Luxembourg counsel or the domiciliation agent to sign the SCSp deed and file with the RCSL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin (signatures legalized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization; the Luxembourg notary may additionally require personal appearance or videoconference identification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and proof of address of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) (passport copy and recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority, utility provider or account-holding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies by the domiciliation agent or notary; underlying identity documents generally do not require a separate apostille for a private-writing SCSp, but do require certified optical/paper verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under the amended Law of 12 November 2004: (i) identify and verify each UBO at the 25% threshold; (ii) determine PEP status of the General Partner and each UBO (art. 3bis; FATF Recommendation 12), applying enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification for PEPs; (iii) screen against EU consolidated sanctions (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and national implementing acts), UN Security Council resolutions, CSSF administrative lists, and, where contractually required by payment rails, OFAC SDN and 50% rule lists; (iv) apply ongoing transaction monitoring and file Suspicious Activity Reports with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) Luxembourg; (v) document risk classification as Low_Risk_Standard with annual reassessment and retention of AML files for five years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – electronic RCSL filing/name search portal at www.lbr.lu; official registry: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filing language is French (prevailing), although German and Luxembourgish are tolerated for names; Latin script is mandatory; foreign-script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The legal form indicator 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must appear in the corporate name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered in the RCSL index, must not infringe third-party intellectual property or trade names, must not mislead as to the company's actual activity, and must not be contrary to public policy or morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit (requires prior CSSF banking license authorization)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SIF / RAIF (requires CSSF notification or specific regulated-fund status)
Bourse / Exchange / Trading Platform (requires Ministry of Finance or CSSF licensing)
Société Nationale / État / Gouvernement (State-sponsored connotation; prior ministerial approval)
Hôpital / Hospital / Clinique (requires Ministry of Health authorization)
Université / Academy (requires Ministry of Higher Education authorization)
Inspection / Testing / Certification (no authorization per se, but must not imply governmental or accreditation status unless ILNAS/OLAS accreditation is actually held)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations may be renewed once for an additional 60 days upon payment of the applicable LBR tariff; thereafter a fresh application is required. Upon rejection by the RCSL conservator, the applicant may (1) request informal administrative re-examination through the LBR portal (response expected within 3 business days); (2) within 15 days of the refusal notification, file a petition before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) under art. 15 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, with mandatory legal representation; and (3) appeal an adverse judgment to the Luxembourg Court of Appeal within 40 days pursuant to arts. 579 et seq. of the New Civil Procedure Code. Concurrently, the applicant should pre-reserve a fallback name to avoid transactional delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible under conditions. The SCSp must maintain a registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg that is accessible to the RCSL, tax authorities and AML/CFT supervisors. A licensed domiciliation agent (agréé) may serve as the statutory registered office; pure virtual arrangements without any local administrative capacity are not compliant. For this cross-border factory pre-shipment QC and inspection agency (ISIC 7120 / NAICS 541380) operating outside Luxembourg's territory, a Luxembourg domiciliation office is commercially and legally acceptable, provided that real decision-making and substance (e.g., management of inspection contracts, invoicing, AML/CFT files) remain traceable in Luxembourg. If the entity performs testing/conformity-assessment activities deemed 'notified body' services within the EU, ILNAS/OLAS accreditation and an actual physical presence are mandatory, with a corporate domiciliation remaining insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 3–5% probability of unannounced inspection in the first fiscal year for a low-risk commercial inspection SCSp; the RCSL, the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and the social security authority may conduct targeted address and substance verifications. If the entity becomes an ILNAS-accredited inspection body, annual witnessed and unannounced surveillance audits raise the likelihood to approximately 10–15% per year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL corporate name availability screening and name reservation (LBR statutory fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by LBR; EUR 14.61 gross inclusive of handling (approximately USD 16)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL incorporation electronic filing with 24-hour processing lane; includes RESA electronic publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: EUR 37.50 gross for 24-hour lane (EUR 16.00 for 4-business-day lane); RESA publication is included in the filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of SCSp constitution and notarial legalization of foreign powers of attorney (optional private-writing form permitted; notarial form required if real estate is contributed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff; standard SCSp incorporation deed market range EUR 700–1,100 plus disbursements; estimated EUR 850 (approximately USD 930)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg counsel - drafting of SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société), due diligence review, and UBO piercing documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg law firm (Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 4,200–5,500 flat fee for a standard SCSp with one corporate general partner; alternative time-based rate EUR 280–450 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office (domiciliation) with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent - first full year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 2,200–2,800 per year; includes registered address, mail handling, reception, and AML client-file support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign General Partner corporate records (Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, MOA, POA) - typically 3 to 5 documents including courier and expediting fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the document origin countries (e.g., U.S. Secretaries of State, U.S. Department of State, foreign ministries, Luxembourg consulates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public fee schedules: apostille USD 10–75 per document; consular legalization varies by jurisdiction; courier USD 100–200; aggregate estimate for 3–5 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translations of foreign corporate documents and UBO identity/proof-of-address (sworn translator)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 60–110 per standard page; estimated 10–12 pages; EUR 750–900 (approximately USD 870)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT PEP and sanctions screening database license (commercial provider) - first year, up to 5 screened individuals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML data provider (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check, ComplyAdvantage equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 150–250 per year for a low-volume single-entity licence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) declaration filing with LBR - mandatory within one month post-incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge under the Law of 13 January 2019; non-compliance subject to criminal fines

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; consolidated taxpayer portal: MyGuichet / eCDF e-filing system (guichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to make taxable supplies in Luxembourg must obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number (TVA number) from the AEDT before commencing activities. Non-established taxable persons are subject to mandatory registration from the first euro of taxable turnover, with no exemption threshold. Procedure: file the VAT registration form (Formulaire 1 – Immatriculation à la TVA) via MyGuichet or directly with the VAT Office together with constitutional documents (partnership agreement, certificate of incorporation of any corporate partner), proof of foreign tax identification for each partner, and the identity of the designated Luxembourg VAT representative where census or fiscal representation is required. For an SCSp, no Luxembourg corporate income tax registration is required at entity level because the partnership is fiscally transparent; the SCSp itself is registered for VAT and for employer-withholding obligations if it employs local staff. The direct tax obligations arise in the hands of the partners according to their own residence and permanent establishment status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default for Luxembourg income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes; profits are allocated to and taxed at partner level. No entity-level election to be treated as an opaque corporation is available for an SCSp. However, the partnership agreement determines the allocation of profit and loss for Luxembourg tax purposes, and partners may elect the applicable territorial allocation of business income. Anti-hybrid rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) must be assessed where the SCSp is treated as a taxable entity in the partner's jurisdiction, potentially triggering disallowance of payments or recharacterization of hybrid mismatches; no unrelated-party hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA) implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 in annual taxable turnover (VAT-exclusive) for taxable persons established in Luxembourg; EUR 0 for foreign/non-established entities, which must register from the first euro of taxable supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and no real-time fiscal clearance, government tax-API, or digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg as of 2025. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies solely to supplies to public-sector contracting authorities via the Peppol BIS 3.0 network under the B2G legal framework. B2B e-invoicing remains optional, subject to authenticity-of-origin, integrity-of-content, and readability requirements. All VAT returns must be filed electronically through the eCDF/MyGuichet portal; VAT invoices issued for export and zero-rating claims must preserve traceable metadata suitable for electronic audit by the AEDT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT (0% with full right to deduct input VAT) applies to: (i) exports of goods dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU in accordance with Article 42 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (ii) intra-Community supplies to taxable persons in another EU Member State holding a valid EU VAT identification number, documented in the quarterly recapitulative statement (RC-list); and (iii) supplies of services for which the place of supply is outside Luxembourg, including on-site pre-shipment inspection and quality-control services physically performed at a factory located in a non-EU country. To claim zero-rating, the exporter must hold robust export evidence demonstrating that the goods left the EU within 90 days (general administrative guidance), and the invoice issued at 0% must reference the statutory exemption basis and, for intra-EU movements, the customer's EU VAT ID.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EXS electronic declaration) accepted by customs authorities and annotated "Exportation" (or the approved export certificate/accusé de dépôt)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent transport document proving that the goods physically left the EU
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract/order matching in description, quantity, and value
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT/wire-transfer banking credit advice evidencing receipt of the full foreign sales proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess unjustified zero-rated export and refund claims within the standard five-year limitation period, extended up to ten years in cases of fraud or significant irregularities. Retrospective clawback is triggered where the export evidence is incomplete, the goods are not demonstrably dispatched within the required timeframe, or the FX proceeds are not received within the 180-day window or from the contractual counterparty. Remedies include VAT correction, statutory late interest accruing monthly, administrative fines of up to 200% of the evaded VAT, criminal fines between EUR 2,500 and EUR 50,000, and, for fraud, imprisonment of the responsible officers. Documentary misdemeanors carry separate civil sanctions, and refund offsets may be suspended pending full substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and financial supervision; foreign exchange administration is effectively delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Economic and Monetary Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member with full capital and current account convertibility under Articles 63-65 TFEU. Profits, dividends, loan repayments, partnership distributions and capital proceeds may be freely repatriated without licence, approval, or surrender requirement. The only practical frictions are standard anti-money laundering documentation and counterparty due diligence. No exchange-control visa or goods-related verification process applies. For an SCSp that is tax-transparent, remittances to non-resident partners are treated as partner-level distributions and remain unrestricted; however, bank-side controls may require a withholding-tax declaration if the SCSp has opted to be treated as opaque for certain tax purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion obligations exist. Export and trade service receipts may be retained in any currency in a Luxembourg-resident account or converted at market rates. The BCL/ECB require statistical reporting under the Balance of Payments (BoP) and International Trade in Services regimes for reporting banks, but no surrender timeline applies. Cross-border payment identification via SWIFT/ISO 20022 is required for statistical and AML purposes only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for operational payment routing and low-value disbursements (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex or other PSD2 electronic money institutions) but Low for capital formation, escrow, and principal relationship banking. Luxembourg law treats EMIs as payment service providers; they may issue IBANs and execute remittances, but cannot grant credit, take deposits, or form the compliance backbone of an SCSp treasury. Use as a secondary clearing or capex-light rail only after confirming the EMI's authorisation in Luxembourg and its access to SWIFT gpi or SEPA Instant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Natural-person directors and ultimate beneficial owners may generally be identified remotely through verified video identification under Luxembourg AML/CFT rules and CSSF guidance, but most tier-1 banks require a physical interview or a formal introduction from an existing relationship officer before opening a capital escrow account for a non-resident SCSp. Operational accounts may be opened via apostilled powers of attorney plus video call, provided the corporate documents and UBO declarations are complete. No universal statutory mandate for physical attendance exists; the bank may impose physical presence under its internal account-opening policy and financial crime risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Deemed high-risk ownership: SCSp with corporate nominee/partnership chain and non-resident LP partners, source of wealth not evidenced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Organisational chart of the full ownership chain to each UBO; 2) certified copy of the partnership deed ('acte constitutif') and RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract; 3) passport copies and proof of residential address for each director/UBO; 4) financial statements or notarised source-of-funds/source-of-wealth statement; 5) enduring bank reference from the existing principal bank; 6) tax residency certificates for foreign partners; 7) a sanctions and negative-news screen report from a professional screening database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance for a pass-through SCSp whose stated scope is low-risk factory inspection and quality control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Executed client service contracts with international manufacturers and inspection standard bodies; 2) invoice pipeline and purchase orders matching projected transaction volumes; 3) office lease or registered-seat document, if any; 4) IFRS/IAS-compliant management accounts; 5) description of outsourced testing/inspection procedures and any statutory auditor certifications; 6) bank references; 7) tax authority acknowledgment (e.g., partnership tax identification number or a written tax-opinion confirmation of transparency).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires to non-EU 'payee-only' jurisdictions or frequent use of fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise) without underlying trade evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Enhanced KYC on each material beneficiary payee: passport, trade licence, bank settlement account confirmation or KYC form; 2) underlying invoices and inspection certificates with date, HS code, site address and client purchase order; 3) end-beneficiary attestation executed by the SCSp manager; 4) internal compliance waiver if the transaction touches a sanctioned corridor; 5) anti-bribery/anti-corruption policy and screening evidence; 6) activity report aligning wire timing with physical inspection dates and site visits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 (for EUR: SEPA Credit Transfer or ISO 20022 pacs.008 via TARGET2) for each capital subscription into the SCSp capital escrow account. Field 70(Remittance Information) must reference the purpose code EQUI for equity injection or INVS for a general investment/capital-account credit; for partner or shareholder loans, use DBTN or INTE as appropriate. The partner's own bank must screen and tag the beneficiary SCSp; the receiving Luxembourg bank will verify the UBO, source-of-funds pack, and partnership deed before posting. Each inbound transfer must be reconciled against the partnership capital ledger and reported to the BCL through the bank's balance-of-payments statistical returns.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Factory-inspection disbursements are service payments to foreign agents, hotels, freight forwarders and subcontracted inspectors. For euro payments to SEPA beneficiaries, use SEPA Credit Transfer, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer, or SWIFT MT103 with purpose code TRAD or INVC. For non-SEPA high-value payments in USD or exotic currencies, send SWIFT MT103 via SWIFT gpi with the correspondent bank KYC pre-approved, including contract number, inspection report date and invoice number. A commercial Letter of Credit is unnecessary for standard QC/testing fees; it is only relevant if the inspection agency also acts as a goods intermediary, which is outside the defined scope. Primary clearing hubs are TARGET2 for EUR, the Eurosystem SEPA rails, and SWIFT gpi for USD/CNY and other currencies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (bilateral ISDA/CSA or master agreement with a Luxembourg bank)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for CNY, TRY, INR and other restricted-convertibility currencies
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term subordinated loans or partnership capital repatriation hedging
FX swaps for liquidity rebalancing between EUR, USD and RMB inflows/outflows
Physical-settlement FX options (OTC) covering a committed underlying inspection-fee exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Luxembourg RCS (mandatory only where the SCSp exceeds the statutory size thresholds; otherwise publication-exempt transparent partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the close of the financial year (for a 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; after formal demand and three months of continued default, RCS may initiate administrative strike-off of the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return of the SCSp (impôt commercial communal) and, where applicable, allocation of allocable profit to the partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Direct Tax Administration of Luxembourg)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by 31 May following the tax year; one additional month if filed electronically through a certified tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge up to EUR 2,500; interest at 0.8% per month on assessed tax; persistent non-filing may produce an official estimation assessment and enforced recovery against partnership assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation and consolidated annual VAT declaration (if the SCSp is registered for VAT on its commercial inspection/testing fees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return due on or before 30 April of the following calendar year; periodic returns (monthly/quarterly) due by the 12th day after the interval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 750; daily interest 0.8% per month; enforcement by distraint against VAT assets; no direct RCS strike-off effect

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation/update in the RBE (trigger-based, no fixed recurring cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change of beneficial owner or partner in the SCSp must be reported within one month; an annual confirmation is triggered only when the annual accounts are approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 250 to EUR 500 and potential six-month custodial sentence for managers; civil daily penalty for continued non-disclosure; administrative non-compliance flagged to the RCS

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is triggered when the transparent SCSp exceeds at least two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000, net turnover EUR 8,800,000, and average workforce of 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts); IFRS optional for unlisted commercial partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An SCSp is a transparent partnership without legal personality; therefore it is not subject to a separate UBO annual confirmation filing. The partnership must file the RBE declaration on activation and update it within one month of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; when the annual accounts are adopted, the managers must review and confirm that the RBE data remains accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (members and capital contributions)
Minute book with recorded resolutions of partners and managers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000 – 18,000 USD per year (waived below statutory audit thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City effective rate (17% national corporate income tax plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus 6.75% average municipal business tax; municipal rates vary by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is a fiscally transparent special limited partnership; absent a taxable election, it is not itself subject to Luxembourg CIT. Profit allocations are taxable only in the hands of partners. No discretionary tax holiday is available. If the SCSp conducts a taxable business in Luxembourg or a taxable election applies, the effective rate is approximately 24.94% with reductions available through the 80% IP box exemption, R&D tax credits, and investment tax credits provided the qualifying activity and substance exist.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry under Luxembourg LIR for corporate income tax loss carryforward; no carryback is permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 / Luxembourg annual corporate income tax declaration (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu or the authorised Luxembourg e-filing platform
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the return for a given tax year is due on 31 May of the following year. A reasoned extension may be requested; the tax administration frequently grants an automatic filing window through 31 December of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward and applicable exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, a non-resident partner does not file Box 1a unless the partner has a Luxembourg permanent establishment or the SCSp is subject to taxable-status treatment; otherwise the partner's allocable share is reportable in the partner's home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward imputation and any carryback claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the transparent SCSp flow through to partners; there is no entity-level loss carryforward unless the SCSp is treated as taxable. A non-resident partner with a Luxembourg PE may carry the allocable Luxembourg loss forward indefinitely in the Luxembourg assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and qualifying tax withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner entitled to domestic or treaty foreign tax credit relief should enter the Luxembourg source taxes borne. Submit the relevant tax residence certificate and detailed computation to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deductions: IP box, investment tax credit, notional interest deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available to persons actually carrying out the Luxembourg activity through a PE; a passive non-resident partner of an SCSp cannot claim these deductions merely because the SCSp has profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a tax increase usually up to 10% of the tax due, monthly late payment interest commonly 0.5% per month, and potential default or estimated assessment. Deliberate failure to file can expose the taxpayer to criminal prosecution for tax fraud with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at SCSp level on profit distributions to partners because the SCSp is tax-transparent and such distributions are not classified as Luxembourg dividends. By contrast, dividends paid by a fully taxable Luxembourg company are subject to statutory Luxembourg withholding tax at 15%, which may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or to 5% under most DTAs for qualifying shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief on any Luxembourg-source payments, the non-resident partner must submit a valid tax residence certificate from its home jurisdiction and complete the applicable Luxembourg relief forms (ordinary procedure via the paying agent or refund procedure with the Luxembourg direct tax administration, ACD). The refund claim must generally be made within the statutory assessment limitation period. For transparent SCSp income, treaty eligibility is determined at partner level; the SCSp itself cannot invoke the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest paid by a Luxembourg taxpayer to foreign recipients, although the EU Interest and Royalties Directive and DTAs generally confirm a 0% rate. Anti-abuse rules apply where the recipient lacks economic substance or the transaction is artificial.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group consolidated revenue is the threshold triggering Luxembourg Local File and Master File requirements, with related-party transactions in aggregate above EUR 1 million generally expected to be documented. Groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million are required to prepare Country-by-Country reporting and file the CbC declaration with the Luxembourg tax authorities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a sectoral Economic Substance Regulation like the UAE, but general tax law, the Luxembourg GAAR, ATAD, and tax-treaty case law require real economic substance. An SCSp engaged in commercial inspection and testing must evidence physical office space, qualified inspectors, equipment, client contracts, decision-making, and bank accounts. Merely passive receipt of testing fees through a shell structure is vulnerable to substance audits, treaty-shopping denial, and reclassification of the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating or omitting taxable profits, fabricating inspection reports, backdating service agreements, destroying records, or falsifying invoices for on-site factory quality control services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax fraud penalties of up to EUR 250,000 fine and up to 5 years imprisonment, plus a tax increase of up to 10% on understated tax, late payment interest, and rescission of favourable tax rulings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner of the SCSp may be criminally prosecuted if they knowingly sign or cause false returns; civil joint and several liability for the tax debt may be imposed; travel restrictions and bank account freezes are possible in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Tax Transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a zero-capital, substance-less SCSp solely to receive inspection agency fees and distribute profits offshore without staff, equipment, or genuine commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the SCSp as taxable, denial of treaty benefits, denial of pass-through treatment, reassessment of profits at the 24.94% combined CIT rate, and penalties for wilful understatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and corporate directors may be personally liable for taxes due if the court pierces the partnership veil; exclusion from serving as manager is possible for culpable conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting the inspection/testing business without AML controls, accepting undocumented cash or unexplained wire transfers, or using the SCSp to conceal the beneficial owner of inspection fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties under Luxembourg AML law that can reach several hundred thousand euros up to EUR 1 million or more for serious breaches, suspension of business authorisation, and criminal money-laundering liability up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers face individual administrative fines; senior officers can be banned from management and criminally prosecuted if money laundering is knowingly aided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Luxembourg Local File, Master File, or CbC report when thresholds are exceeded, or pricing intercompany quality-control service charges in a non-arm's length manner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reallocation of profit to Luxembourg, additional tax at 24.94%, late interest, and potentially a 10% penalty on the additional assessment for missing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing declarations may face individual administrative fines; personal civil liability may attach if the transaction is found to be a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a commercial inspection and testing business without the required statutory licence or issuing pre-shipment inspection certificates without actual testing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Operating without licence attracts fines, closure orders, and disqualification from public accreditation; invoice fraud triggers additional tax penalties and criminal prosecution for forgery/fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner may be personally liable for fines, restitution to clients, and criminal punishment including imprisonment for fraudulent commercial practices.
